title: Hall, yard and zones overview
before:
1. The Harborwick site centres on a single warehouse hall covering 6,000 m2, with an adjoining outdoor yard for manoeuvring and parking. Learn the hall perimeter, the yard entrances and the marked internal routes before starting work.
2. Eight dock doors serve the building on one facade. Dock doors 1-4 are assigned to inbound receiving, while dock doors 5-8 are assigned to outbound dispatch, including 4 outbound dock doors available for loading.
3. Zone A forms the receiving zone at inbound docks 1-4. All unloading and goods inspection takes place there, and inbound vehicles are marshalled to those four doors only.
4. From Zone A, approved stock moves directly into storage. Zone B provides bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, which offers 2,400 pallet positions across the high bays.
5. Zone C operates as the picking zone. It contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks arranged for short travel and scanner-directed work, separate from the high-bay reserve in Zone B.
6. Zone D provides the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Build and check outbound loads there, keeping each door apron clear for the next trailer.
7. Zone E is the cold zone for chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Access is restricted to assigned tasks, and doors are kept closed except for put-away and retrieval.
8. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Inside Zone F, a fenced hazmat cage covers 60 m2 for segregated storage, alongside the designated areas for quarantine and rework.
9. Main transport aisles through the hall measure 4.0 m wide. Keep them free of pallets, waste and staged stock at all times to allow two-way truck movement.
10. Rack storage aisles between the high bays measure 3.0 m wide. Enter them only when authorised, observe priority signs, and never stage pallets inside the aisle profile.
11. Pedestrian routes cross the hall at defined points and connect all zones A-F. Use only those routes when moving on foot, remain clear of truck swept paths, and report any blocked or faded markings.
12. Memorise the zone sequence from goods-in to goods-out: Zone A for receiving at doors 1-4, Zone B for bulk storage, Zone C for picking, Zone D for dispatch at doors 5-8, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F for value-added services including the hazmat cage.

title: Put-away process
before:
1. Execute PR-02 Put-away to storage for every pallet released from receiving and move only system-booked goods to their storage destination.

2. Confirm in the WMS that inbound goods were inspected before booking, because inspection always precedes system booking, and never start put-away when the booking receipt is missing or incomplete.

3. Release pallets to put-away strictly after system booking, since goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage, and return any unbooked pallet to receiving for completion of the inbound steps.

4. Assign Forklift operators to all put-away transport, as Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks, and select the truck type that suits the pallet weight, height and destination aisle.

5. Direct ambient bulk pallets to Zone B, noting that Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, and follow the WMS location instruction for aisle, bay and level without substituting an alternative position.

6. Transport chilled pallets immediately to Zone E, noting that Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, and minimise door-open and staging time to protect the temperature range.

7. Deliver pallets requiring labelling, kitting, inspection or other special treatment to Zone F, noting that Zone F holds the value-added services area, and hand over each pallet to the responsible staff at the defined drop point.

8. Scan every put-away at the destination location and verify that the WMS confirms the correct zone and position for Zone B, Zone E or Zone F.

9. Report missing labels, unreadable barcodes, damaged pallets or occupied locations immediately and leave the pallet in a safe holding position until the system instruction is corrected.

10. Close PR-02 Put-away to storage in the WMS only after all pallets from the booking have a confirmed storage location, thereby keeping booked stock, physical location and system inventory fully aligned for replenishment and picking.

11. Keep put-away lanes and staging areas clear during the operation and return handling equipment to its parking position once the last pallet of the booking is stored.

title: Cold storage in Zone E
before:
1. Hold all chilled stock only in Zone E in line with PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
2. Maintain Zone E within its chilled range at all times during storage and put-away.
3. Verify the cold-zone temperature manually each shift and record the reading.
4. Prioritise cold-chain pallets at put-away and minimise time outside Zone E.
5. Segregate non-conforming chilled stock immediately and escalate under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Do not use Zone E for ambient, quarantine or general bulk overflow. Keep the boundary to the rest of the warehouse closed except for direct put-away, replenishment and collection moves.

6. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C. Treat any reading below +2 °C as a breach.
7. Keep the cold zone at or below +8 °C. Treat any reading above +8 °C as a breach.
8. Check the fixed display on entry and confirm it with the manual verification for the shift.
9. Log each shift verification with time and initials in the designated record.
10. Re-verify after any prolonged door opening, defrost cycle or maintenance work.

Manual verification each shift is mandatory and does not replace continuous monitoring where fitted. Never rely on memory or on the previous shift reading. Record the actual observed value at the time of the check and sign for it.

11. Move chilled inbound pallets to Zone E without delay after release from receiving.
12. Transport chilled goods in closed load units and do not stage them in ambient aisles.
13. Rotate chilled stock by expiry date and keep labels visible for scanner tasks.
14. Leave air circulation gaps around pallets and do not block coolers or sensors.
15. Keep Zone E floors dry, clear of packaging waste and free of ice build-up.

Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every receipt, put-away, replenishment, pick and return that touches chilled product. Follow its steps for temperature evidence, time limits outside the chamber and handling of insulated containers. Where PR-12 Cold-chain handling requires a hold, place the stock on hold and prevent further picking until release.

16. Stop normal put-away into Zone E on any temperature breach and contain stock already inside.
17. Quarantine product exposed to out-of-range conditions pending a documented decision.
18. Report every breach, probe failure and missing shift check without delay for review.
19. Do not release breached chilled stock to picking, packing or dispatch without authorisation.
20. Restore the +2 to +8 °C range and prove stability with a fresh verification before resuming normal moves.

Discipline in Zone E protects product safety and stock accuracy. Maintain the +2 to +8 °C envelope, verify it manually each shift, work strictly to PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and keep full records to show the cold chain was never broken.

title: Cold-chain and hazmat controls
before:
1. Execute PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all chilled stock movements, storage and temperature checks without exception.
2. Maintain Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C for all temperature-controlled inventory.
3. Verify the Zone E temperature manually each shift with the calibrated display and site thermometer.
4. Record each shift reading immediately in the temperature log with time and initials.
5. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
6. Keep the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
7. Close Zone E doors promptly after every entry and exit to protect the +2 to +8 °C range.
8. Isolate any pallet showing temperature abuse and escalate it under PR-12 Cold-chain handling before further movement.
9. Prohibit staging chilled pallets outside Zone E except for immediate loading or put-away under active control.
10. Execute PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all classified hazardous goods, storage checks and spill actions.
11. Store all hazmat only inside the fenced hazmat cage inside Zone F, never in general racking or open floor areas.
12. Limit total holdings in the hazmat cage to no more than 4,000 kg at one time across all SKUs and containers.
13. Plan cage occupancy on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.
14. Check cage stock weight before every put-away and reject any receipt that would exceed 4,000 kg.
15. Keep incompatible classes segregated within the cage according to label instructions and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Inspect containers, bunds, labels and extinguishers each shift and clear any obstruction from cage access and spill kits.
17. Contain drips immediately, ventilate the area, don the specified protective equipment and notify supervision under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
18. Forbid ignition sources, food and unauthorised entry inside the cage and ensure spill residues leave only through the approved waste route.

title: Cold zone rules
before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every pallet, carton and tote stored in Zone E.

Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Treat any deviation from that band as a cold-chain failure, not as a local fluctuation. Never store ambient, frozen or uncontrolled goods in Zone E to save space or time.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times.

Monitor door openings, defrost cycles and loading dwell times because each one drives temperature downward or disrupts airflow. Keep the doors closed except for active put-away, replenishment or loading, and report icing, pooling water or uneven cooling without delay.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times.

During warm weather, frequent access or equipment heat can push the upper limit quickly. Limit personnel entry to assigned tasks, switch off idle handling equipment inside the chamber, and escalate any upward trend before the limit is reached.

4. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift.

Use the calibrated display and the manual check defined in PR-12 Cold-chain handling, then record the reading, time and your name in the designated log. Across shift changes, communicate the last verified reading and any door or plant faults as part of handover.

5. Wear mandatory protection before entering Zone E.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including all work inside the cold zone. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, including wet or cold floors in Zone E. Add suitable thermal layers and gloves for prolonged chilled work, keeping cuffs, laces and hems clear of pallets and rollers.

6. Control movements and behaviour inside the chilled area.

Walk at a steady pace on potentially slippery surfaces, use handrails where provided, and never run to warm up. Handle chilled cartons with dry hands or appropriate gloves, stack them stably, and clean up condensation or spillages immediately to prevent slips.

7. Protect product integrity during every transfer.

Plan picks and put-aways so chilled goods remain inside Zone E until the moment of movement. Stage outbound chilled pallets only for immediate loading and return inbound chilled pallets to Zone E without intermediate storage in ambient areas.

8. Escalate alarms, suspect stock and equipment faults immediately.

Notify the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, of any temperature alarm, door failure, refrigeration fault, or pallet that feels warm, thawed or damp. Isolate suspect stock as directed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and prevent its picking, packing or dispatch until cleared.

9. Keep accountability for cold-chain safety unambiguous.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including calibration, maintenance priorities and final decisions on temperature-abused stock. The shift supervisor controls chilled work on the shift, enforces PR-12 Cold-chain handling, confirms each manual verification, and ensures only fit staff work extended periods in low temperatures.

title: Shift Supervisors
before:
1. Run one assigned shift in full charge of floor staff and incident response.
2. Direct Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, according to roster.
3. Report to the warehouse manager, who remains accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
4. Allocate inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns staff, maintenance support and dispatch activity for the shift.
5. Supervise Zone A, the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
6. Supervise Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
7. Supervise Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
8. Supervise Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
9. Supervise Zone E, the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
10. Supervise Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
11. Enforce mandatory high-visibility vests for everyone on the warehouse floor.
12. Enforce mandatory safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor.
13. Review every incident report arising on the shift and direct immediate containment, first response and escalation.
14. Lead evacuation under PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
15. Control the quarterly evacuation drill on shift, account for all personnel at the assembly point and ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
16. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
17. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval before any system posting.
18. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling, confirming restock, rework or scrap.
19. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change of shift and remain accountable until the incoming shift supervisor has accepted the floor in person.
20. Brief the incoming supervisor on labour, equipment status, overdue orders, cold-zone integrity, quarantine holdings, incidents and open safety actions.

During the shift the supervisor stays visible on the floor, prioritises safety over throughput and stops any unsafe operation. Absences, equipment faults and zone congestion are rebalanced across Zones A to F without delaying outbound commitments. All decisions, approvals and incident reviews are recorded in the shift log for traceability.

title: Inbound Operators
before:
1. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving from document check to system booking.

Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Operators report for their assigned shift, either Shift 1 which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

2. Before any trailer is opened, verify the booking, delivery note and purchase order quantity against the scheduled load.

At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading. Do not start unloading where documents are missing, quantities disagree or damage is visible from outside until the exception has been escalated under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

3. During unloading, count every carton and pallet, check outer packaging condition, labels and expiry dates where applicable, and segregate quantity variances and visible damage.

Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system. Record inspection results in the WMS and on the delivery paperwork without delay.

4. Operate pallet handling equipment within the receiving area to move inbound pallets to inspection and booking lanes, keeping pedestrian routes and dock approaches clear at all times.

Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Sign out a scanner at shift start, confirm each booking scan, and return the unit for charging at shift end.

5. Book inspected goods into the system immediately after inspection, print or activate pallet labels, and confirm weight and dimensions.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Reject overweight or unstable pallets for rework before booking.

6. Stage booked pallets by destination for release to PR-02 Put-away to storage.

Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Direct general pallets for Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Direct chilled pallets for Zone E, which is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Direct value-added, quarantine and returns-related receipts for Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

7. Hand over staged stock to forklift operators for put-away only after system booking is complete, ensuring each pallet carries its identifier and destination.

Never release unbooked goods to storage aisles or dispatch areas.

8. Wear prescribed personal protective equipment throughout all receiving work.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

9. Work under the direction of the shift team structure at all times.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow tasking, report variances, damage and missing documents immediately, and request reassignment before leaving Zone A. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

title: Temperature-Controlled Storage
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. provides chilled storage in Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C for client stock requiring continuous temperature control.
2. Within Zone E the Client may rely on maintenance of the full compliant band at all times, with lower protection at or above +2 °C and upper protection at or below +8 °C without interruption.
3. All chilled operations are executed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling, which governs receipt, storage, monitoring and escalation for every pallet held in the cold zone.
4. Upon arrival chilled inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system, and temperature condition, packaging integrity and documentation form part of that inspection.
5. Following acceptance, goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage, ensuring system traceability precedes any physical transfer to Zone E.
6. Put-away into chilled locations is performed under PR-02 Put-away to storage in coordination with PR-12 Cold-chain handling, preserving cold-chain continuity during transfer.
7. During every shift Harborwick manually verifies cold-zone temperature each shift and records the verified reading for audit and client reporting.
8. Continuous monitoring supplements the manual verification, and any excursion below +2 °C or above +8 °C triggers immediate containment, notification and documented corrective action under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
9. Affected chilled pallets remain isolated in Zone E pending assessment, and no compromised stock is released for order fulfilment without agreed disposition.
10. For transparency the Client receives shift verification records and excursion reports on request, with storage temperature history traceable by location and time period.
11. Harborwick commits to maintain Zone E capacity, calibrated monitoring equipment and trained personnel sufficient to sustain the +2 to +8 °C commitment across all contracted chilled volumes.
